causes.text: Analysts projected that U.S. car sales would decline sharply in the first quarter of 2022 because parts shortages, soaring gasoline prices and rising interest rates were squeezing consumers and automakers, with J.D. Power forecasting an 18% drop from a year earlier.

source_info.title: U.S. auto sales set to plunge as parts shortages and high gas prices bite

effects.text: BMW reported a 12% rise in fourth-quarter earnings for 2022-2023 but missed analysts' expectations; shares fell as much as 3.7% because rising inflation and higher interest rates dampened demand, despite improved chip supply.

source_info.title: BMW earnings lag some estimates, names new finance chief

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Parts shortages, high fuel prices and rising interest rates led analysts to predict a sharp decline in U.S. auto sales, signalling weakened consumer demand and higher financing costs.
Persistently high inflation and interest rates throughout 2022 and early 2023 reduced consumers' purchasing power across major markets, dampening demand for premium vehicles like BMW's.
BMW's fourth-quarter results missed some analysts' expectations; investors reacted to the demand slowdown and the stock slipped roughly 3.7% on the day of the announcement.

rationale: Macroeconomic pressures-namely supply shortages, fuel price spikes and higher interest rates-reduced consumer demand for new cars. BMW, as a premium automaker, faced softer orders and thus posted earnings below expectations.
counterfactual_analysis: If energy prices and interest rates had remained stable, consumer purchasing power would have been stronger and BMW might have delivered earnings more in line with or above analyst forecasts.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Continued disruptions may have limited vehicle availability, independently contributing to lower sales and earnings

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Inflation, higher interest rates and fuel costs squeezing auto demand
details.commentary: Rising borrowing and fuel costs reduced households' ability and willingness to buy new vehicles, even as supply bottlenecks eased. Those macro pressures carried through to BMW's results, where softer demand and cautious outlook commentary led investors to focus on downside risks despite headline profit growth.
